sub_area: OAuth2 base test case with sid cookie login helper
rationale: Base class providing session/sid-based HTTP helpers for OAuth2 tests; ferro has no session auth and does not implement OAuth2 endpoints. OAuth is an intentionally absent subsystem.

sub_area: OAuth2 authorization code, PKCE, token revoke, implicit, OpenID Connect flows
rationale: Tests the full OAuth2/OpenID Connect flow via Frappe's Python integration layer (oauth2.authorize, get_token, revoke_token, openid_profile); ferro does not implement any OAuth2 endpoints and this is an intentionally absent subsystem.

sub_area: Password hashing (pbkdf2), encrypted field storage, Fernet encrypt/decrypt, rename/delete propagation in __Auth
rationale: Encodes the password storage contract (pbkdf2_sha256 hash in __Auth, Fernet-encrypted passwords) that ferro's crypto.rs and auth.rs must match; ferro implements pbkdf2 verification and Fernet decrypt but not the full encrypted-field lifecycle (rename, delete propagation) which is Python-only.

sub_area: Password strength checker performance (zxcvbn timing bound)
rationale: Pure in-process test of frappe.utils.password_strength (zxcvbn wrapper); ferro does not implement a password strength checker and this is a Python utility concern entirely outside ferro's scope.

sub_area: Patch module discovery, patch list integrity, Patch Log count vs patches.txt
rationale: Tests the Frappe patch/migration system (patches.txt parsing, Patch Log records); ferro implements its own md5-gated schema migration but never exposes patch execution over HTTP. This is dev/install tooling ferro does not replicate.

sub_area: patches.txt parser: empty file, sections, old-style, edge cases, comment handling
rationale: Unit tests for the patch.txt file parser (mock_open-based); purely internal Python tooling with no HTTP surface and no relevance to ferro's runtime.

sub_area: PDF generation: margin CSS parsing, encryption, private images, wkhtmltopdf/weasyprint integration
rationale: Tests Frappe's PDF generation pipeline (pdfgen, wkhtmltopdf/weasyprint) which ferro intentionally does not implement; PDF rendering is a Python-only subsystem.

sub_area: CPython-side performance: query count, meta caching, redis caching, memory, RPS via FrappeClient
rationale: MariaDB-only performance regression tests measuring CPython Frappe's internal caching and query counts; the RPS test uses FrappeClient with password/session auth which ferro does not support, and all assertions are benchmarks of CPython internals irrelevant to ferro.

sub_area: HTTP overhead: Redis and SQL call counts for ping and list/get endpoints
rationale: Uses FrappeAPITestCase to count Redis and SQL calls per HTTP request (ping, resource list, get); ferro has no Redis and its SQL call count differs structurally, so exact overhead numbers don't apply, but ferro must respond correctly to these endpoints — also gated MariaDB-only so skipped on SQLite.

sub_area: Role-based and user-permission-based read/write/create/delete access, if_owner, permlevel, set_only_once, strict user permissions
rationale: Encodes the full Frappe permission model (role perms, user permissions, if_owner, perm levels, strict mode) that ferro's auth.rs and orm.rs partially implement; ferro handles role-based read/write gating but lacks user-permission filtering, if_owner enforcement, and permlevel masking — this test suite defines the contract ferro must approach.

sub_area: Print view HTML rendering, permission check on cancelled docs
rationale: Tests frappe.www.printview.get_html_and_style which is Jinja/HTML rendering in CPython; ferro does not implement print view rendering and this is an intentionally absent subsystem.

sub_area: frappe/__init__.py LOC budget enforcement
rationale: Purely a code-quality gate that counts lines in frappe/__init__.py; no runtime behavior is tested and no HTTP surface is involved — entirely irrelevant to ferro.

sub_area: frappe.qb.get_query: SQL generation, field validation (SELECT/WHERE injection prevention), filters with linked doctypes, tree queries, perm-gated get_list
rationale: Tests the query builder's SQL generation and filter validation which encode ORM filter semantics ferro must replicate in orm.rs; ferro uses its own filter parsing rather than frappe.qb but must produce equivalent safe queries — field injection prevention and perm-gated list results are behaviors ferro's REST list endpoint must match.

sub_area: MariaDB-specific SQL functions: GROUP_CONCAT, MATCH/AGAINST, ConstantColumn, TIMESTAMP, CombineDatetime
rationale: MariaDB-only tests of Frappe's Python query builder SQL function generation; ferro targets SQLite only and uses its own SQL generation — these MariaDB-specific function tests have no relevance to ferro.

sub_area: PostgreSQL-specific SQL functions: STRING_AGG, TSVECTOR, timestamp arithmetic
rationale: PostgreSQL-only tests of Frappe's Python query builder; ferro targets SQLite and these Postgres-specific generated SQL forms are irrelevant to ferro's runtime.

sub_area: Query builder: tab prefix, run() patcher, aggregate functions (max/min/avg/sum)
rationale: Abstract mixin testing Frappe's Python query builder internals (tab prefix, run patcher, aggregates); ferro has its own SQL layer and does not use frappe.qb — these are internal Python ORM builder tests with no HTTP surface.

sub_area: Query builder parameterization: %(param)s substitution in WHERE/SET/CASE expressions
rationale: Tests Frappe's Python query builder's named-parameter injection prevention mechanism; ferro uses its own SQL parameter binding in Rust and does not use frappe.qb, making these tests irrelevant to ferro's runtime.

sub_area: MariaDB query builder: tab prefix in FROM clause, get_query_builder factory
rationale: MariaDB-specific query builder tests; ferro targets SQLite only and does not use frappe.qb, so these are irrelevant to ferro's runtime.

sub_area: PostgreSQL query builder: tab prefix, schema replacement, field name aliasing
rationale: PostgreSQL-specific query builder tests; ferro targets SQLite only and does not use frappe.qb, so these are entirely irrelevant to ferro's runtime.

sub_area: Query builder misc: custom functions, schema-qualified functions, Table utility, UNION queries
rationale: Tests miscellaneous Frappe Python query builder utilities (ParameterizedFunction, Table, UNION); ferro has its own SQL layer and these internal Python builder tests have no HTTP surface relevant to ferro.

sub_area: IN operator handling: null/empty value coalescing, func_in SQL generation
rationale: Tests how Frappe's query builder handles IN filters with null/empty values (IS NULL expansion); ferro's orm.rs must implement equivalent IN-filter null handling when processing REST API filter parameters, but the SQL generation mechanism differs.

sub_area: Query Report: xlsx export, CSV export, duplicate column names, script reports, email export, xlsx style builder
rationale: Tests Frappe's report execution and export pipeline (xlsx, csv, email) which ferro intentionally does not implement; reports and print/export are Python-only subsystems outside ferro's scope.
